chunks: 4894 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Aban, from Ghiyath, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding an impotent man: if it is known that he is impotent and does not approach women, they are to be separated. But if he has intercourse with her even once, they are not to be separated. And a man is not rejected on account of a defect.

key_terms.الْعِنِّينِ: an impotent man incapable of sexual intercourse
key_terms.عَيْبٍ: a defect or physical flaw in the legal context
key_terms.عُلِمَ: it is established or known with certainty

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on separation from an impotent husband in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning an impotent husband in marriage. If his impotence is established and he is unable to have intercourse, separation is ruled; but if intercourse occurs even once, separation is not ruled on that basis. It also states that a man is not rejected due to a defect.
